questions: Have your walking or balance problems progressively worsened over time?
Did you begin having repeated falls early in the illness?
Do you have difficulty looking down when asked, such as when reading or stepping off a curb?
Do you have difficulty looking up when asked?
Do your eyes sometimes fail to move promptly toward something you are trying to look at?
Do you experience double vision?
Have you noticed unusual blinking, prolonged eye closure, or difficulty opening your eyelids?
Have you become noticeably slower or stiffer in your movements?
Have you developed difficulty speaking clearly or swallowing?
Have family or friends noticed changes in your judgment, personality, motivation, or behavior?
Do you have problems with memory or planning?
Do you have slurred speech or difficulty coordinating your hands?
Do you feel numbness or reduced sensation in your feet?
Do you feel faint or light-headed when standing up?
Have you developed urinary urgency, urinary retention, or loss of bladder control?
Have you had constipation or sexual difficulties that began after your walking problems?
Have you had episodes of sudden weakness, loss of awareness, or other abrupt neurological symptoms?
Does anyone in your family have a similar walking, balance, or coordination disorder?
Do you take medications that can cause drowsiness, unsteadiness, or abnormal movements?
Do you regularly drink large amounts of alcohol?
orders: Comprehensive bedside neurologic examination with gait testing during distraction, dual-tasking, tandem walking, and assessment for variability, inconsistency, and entrainment.
Detailed bedside ocular-motor examination, including saccades, smooth pursuit, optokinetic nystagmus, vestibulo-ocular reflex, and convergence.
Bedside cerebellar examination, including finger–nose, heel–shin, rapid alternating movements, truncal stability, and rebound testing.
Standardized pull test and assessment of postural responses.
MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted, susceptibility-weighted, and contrast-enhanced sequences.
Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, thyroid-stimulating hormone, vitamin B12, folate, vitamin E, copper, ceruloplasmin, and hemoglobin A1c.
Serum drug and toxin screen, including sedative-hypnotics and anticonvulsants.
Video-oculography with vestibular testing, including caloric or video head-impulse testing.
